19 A wire is fixed at one end and extended by a force that is applied to the other end. The force is
slowly increased from zero and then slowly decreased back to zero.
The force–extension graph for the wire is shown.
force
extension
0
0
The graph line for the wire being loaded is the same as the graph line for the wire being
unloaded.
Which statement describes the deformation of the wire?
A
It is both elastic and plastic.
B
It is elastic only.
C
It is neither elastic nor plastic.
D
It is plastic only.

hints: Look at where the unloading arrow ends on the extension axis when the force has fallen back to zero.
Connect that end point to the physics: elastic means full recovery to zero extension, plastic means a permanent extension remains.
Check whether the curved upper part of the force-extension line changes that test, given that loading and unloading follow the same line.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: the force-extension graph starts at the origin, curves at larger force, and the unloading line retraces the loading line exactly back to the origin.

State the rule: elastic deformation is reversed completely when the force is removed, so extension $x = 0$ when force $F = 0$; plastic deformation leaves a permanent extension, so $x > 0$ when $F = 0$.
Apply the rule to this graph: at the end of unloading, $F = 0$ and $x = 0$, so there is no residual extension.
Note that the curvature at the top does not create plastic deformation here; it only shows non-linear elastic behaviour because the return path is identical with no hysteresis loop.
Therefore the deformation is fully recovered and is elastic only. This is option B

A.explanation: There is no permanent extension because unloading returns along the same line to zero extension, so plastic deformation has not occurred.

B.explanation: The wire returns to zero extension when force returns to zero, which is the definition of elastic deformation with no plastic part.

C.explanation: The wire does show elastic behaviour because it fully recovers its original length on unloading.

D.explanation: Plastic deformation would leave a residual extension at zero force, but the graph returns to the origin.
